description: Train your AI self, amplify you, bridge the world

summary.one_liner: Second Me is an open-source prototype for training a local AI "self" on your own memories, which can then be hosted on your machine and optionally connected to a wider network.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a system for building a personal AI identity trained on your own memories, using Hierarchical Memory Modeling (HMM) and a Me-Alignment Algorithm. Training and hosting are described as local, with the model running on your own hardware. The README says the AI self can be launched onto a decentralized "Second Me Network," where other apps or people can connect with your permission to access your shared context. It also mentions two example app modes: Roleplay, where the AI switches personas to represent you, and AI Space, where multiple Second Mes collaborate. Deployment is via Docker (make docker-up) or an integrated non-Docker setup, with model size guidance based on available memory. The README mentions MLX acceleration for Mac M-series users (CLI-only). Base models are from the Qwen2.5 series and inference uses llama.cpp; GraphRAG from Microsoft is used for data synthesis.
use_cases: train a personal AI that mimics my own voice and memories
run a local private AI assistant on my own hardware
let apps query my AI identity with my permission
roleplay as me in different scenarios
have multiple personal AIs collaborate on ideas
experiment with memory-based fine-tuning of small local models
how_to_run: Open the web interface in your browser (URL is not shown in the README text)
For integrated (non-Docker) setup, see the Deployment Guide on GitBook
notable: Hierarchical Memory Modeling (HMM) and Me-Alignment Algorithm for training on personal memories
Local training and hosting, with optional connection to a decentralized network
Permission-based sharing of your context with other apps or AI selves
Roleplay persona switching and multi-AI 'AI Space' collaboration modes
Hardware guidance table mapping RAM to supported model sizes for Docker and integrated setups
caveats: Hardware demands: model size is limited by available memory, and models below 0.5B may perform poorly on complex tasks
Cross-platform support is described as ongoing; OS-specific compatibility issues may occur
Some features (the network, continuous training, cloud training/deployment) are described as roadmap or future items rather than current functionality
